https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Grade Requirement
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Major grades and progression
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: Yeshiva College requires a major GPA of at least 2.000, at least C- in every course counted toward the major, and at least C- in prerequisites to advance. The university also requires an overall GPA of 2.000; this is context, not a complete degree audit.

https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Residency
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Major residence and individual transfer review
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: At least 60% of the major/minor must be completed in residence for the standard entry route and, generally, for transfer students. Transfer students must consult an adviser about their applicable residency requirements. Additional degree-wide residence rules depend on entry history; no single degree-wide credit threshold is assigned to this concentration.

https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Declaration of Major/Change of Major
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Major declaration and catalog applicability
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: Declare a major through the Registrar by 60 earned credits, including transferred credits; undeclared students may receive a registration hold. Use the Declaration of Academic Major and Minors form. A change follows the catalog of the change year, may be filed once per registration period without adviser approval, and cannot follow a graduation application. A separate AI concentration declaration procedure is not established by this general policy.

https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Pass/No Credit (P/N)
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Letter grades for required courses
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: For Yeshiva College on the Wilf Campus, P grades cannot satisfy major/minor requirements or required major correlates. P/N is limited to free electives for students beyond freshman year in good standing; it does not replace the required concentration course grades.

https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Course Substitutions
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Written substitution approval
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: An academic adviser may authorize a substitute course in writing after approval from the department chair or dean’s office. A substitution is an individual decision, not an additional published concentration option.

https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Courses at Outside Institutions
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Prior approval for outside coursework
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: Obtain school approval and the appropriate outside-course request form before enrollment, normally only in summer. Supply a syllabus unless the course is pre-approved. Community-college and unaccredited courses are not approved. Approved courses need at least C; grades do not enter the YU GPA. Summer courses last at least four weeks. Session credit caps are 4/7/8/9/10 for sessions lasting 4/5/6/7/8 weeks, with at most 10 credits across the summer. Quarter conversion is 4 credits to 2.5 YU credits or 5 to 3. Department-specific CS/math summer approval still applies.

https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Transfer Credit Policies
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Transfer evaluation is individual
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: After admission, prior courses require an official transcript and a full syllabus for evaluation. YU normally accepts aligned courses from regionally accredited institutions with at least C; acceptance is individually determined. Current students need prior adviser approval. High-school college coursework has a separate bachelor’s limit of nine credits and B- minimum, requires official transcripts during admission and syllabi, and does not meet residence requirements. Experiential-learning transfer credit is not awarded to students admitted from Fall 2024.

https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Prerequisite and Corequisite Policy
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Prerequisite and corequisite compliance
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: A prerequisite precedes the dependent course; a corequisite is taken concurrently, and a concurrent prerequisite permits either timing. Students earning below C- in a prerequisite may be removed from the subsequent course. Individual requisites must be checked in the course description in Self Service.

https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.heading: Course Share
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.title: Course overlap requires department policy
https://yu.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current.summary: Ordinarily one course may count between general education and a major/minor. Credit-intensive programs may permit more under their department’s policy. Departments also set sharing rules between majors/minors. This general rule is not a numerical cap on the AI track’s published math-minor overlap.
